q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-18. Q2 FY2027 ends on July 31, 2026 (NVIDIA's fiscal Q2 ends at the end of July). The earnings release was May 20, 2026, which provided *forward guidance* for Q2 FY2027. 

The resolution asks: "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release?"

This is asking what guidance NVIDIA provides when they report Q2 FY2027 results. That earnings release would occur in late August 2026 (typically 4-5 weeks after quarter end). Given today is 2026-08-18, the Q2 FY2027 earnings release is imminent — likely within days.

**Time left: approximately 0-14 days**

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for forward guidance provided in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release (guidance for Q3 FY2027, presumably).

Key facts from current research:
- Q1 FY2027 revenue: $81.6 billion (actual)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance from Q1 earnings: $91.0 billion ±2% = $89.2B to $92.8B range
- Analyst consensus for Q2 FY2027: $91.846 billion
- Recent quarter growth: 20% sequential, 85% YoY

NVIDIA has shown strong sequential growth (20% Q1→Q2). The midpoint of provided guidance ($91.0B) would represent 11.5% sequential growth from Q1.

For Q3 FY2027 forward guidance (what will be announced at the Q2 earnings release):
- If the company maintains momentum and continues data center growth
- Historical pattern shows NVIDIA providing conservative guidance they can beat
- The analyst consensus at $91.8B suggests modest upside to the $91.0B midpoint

Assuming Q2 FY2027 comes in near or slightly above guidance (~$91B), forward guidance for Q3 would likely be in the $95-105B range, reflecting continued but potentially moderating sequential growth (4-14% sequential growth).

The midpoint of the given range is $107.5B. This would represent about 18% sequential growth from the expected ~$91B Q2, which seems plausible given:
- NVIDIA's strong AI momentum
- Data center market strength
- But also accounting for normal seasonal patterns and potential moderation

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Macro deterioration or AI sentiment shift
- Unexpected competition or demand weakness
- Supply chain constraints
- China restrictions impacting business more than expected
- Seasonal weakness (Q3 is typically less strong than Q2)
- Conservative guidance reset if Q2 comes in significantly above expectations
- Market saturation concerns in key verticals

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected Q2 results
- Accelerating AI adoption and data center buildout
- New product cycles (Blackwell ramp continuing)
- Surprise wins in new markets or customer segments
- Guidance raise if Q2 substantially beats the $91B midpoint
- Continued geopolitical support from US policy
- Better macro environment

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027: $81.6B actual
- Q2 FY2027: $91.0B guided midpoint (±2%)
- Sequential growth Q1→Q2: ~11.5%
- YoY growth: 85%

The range given (99.5 to 115.5B) is relatively tight around a midpoint of 107.5B. This represents:
- ~18% sequential growth from expected Q2 of ~$91B
- ~31% YoY growth (if Q3 FY2026 was ~$78B)

This seems reasonable but perhaps slightly optimistic given:
- Normal moderation of growth rates at scale
- Q3 can be seasonally weaker than Q2
- The guidance would need to show confidence in sustained high growth

However, NVIDIA's track record of beating guidance and strong AI momentum could justify this level.

## My estimate

The most likely range is $100-108B, with concentration around $102-106B. This represents:
- ~11-17% sequential growth from Q2's expected ~$91B
- Conservative but reasonable guidance
- Consistent with NVIDIA's pattern of providing beatable guidance

The range endpoints (99.5-115.5B) suggest forecasters see meaningful uncertainty around whether Q3 guidance will be more conservative or more aggressive.

Given the strength shown in Q1→Q2 (11.5% guidance, likely to be beaten), Q3 guidance of ~104-105B seems most probable.

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's Q1 FY2027 earnings release on May 20, 2026, already provided forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue. NVIDIA expects Q2 FY2027 revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027/). This guidance excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

Analysts' consensus revenue estimate for Q2 FY2027 is slightly higher at $91.846 billion [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors). This guidance follows a record Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6 billion, up 20% from the previous quarter and 85% year-over-year [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).
